newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka military pushes deserters to return.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka military pushes deserters to return.

text.p: Sri Lanka warned deserters from its depleted armed forces that an amnesty allowing them to return to barracks expired on Saturday.
The military has said it will crack down on deserters who failed to respond, but has so far not indicated what punishment awaits them.

"Those deserters who have not yet reported, but wish to avail themselves of this amnesty, can do so before midnight on November 30," a statement issued by the defence ministry's operational headquarters said.
Military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters the amnesty, which has been extended several times, was "not likely" to be stretched further.
Forcing deserters to return to barracks is part of the military's plan to beef up the forces, who have been fighting the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam for 13 years.

According to defence ministry figures, about 15,000 soldiers have deserted during the past five years as fighting escalated with the rebels, who are seeking an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Army officials said they were unsure how many deserters had reported for duty, but that the army planned to get back 10,000 to 12,000.
"People have responded very well (to the amnesty) during the past couple of weeks. Many have surrendered," Jayatunga said.
The army has also warned firms against employing deserters.
"Those who harbour or employ deserters are also reminded that it is an offence to do so and are advised to release any such deserters in their employ," the defence ministry statement said.
